subject: Hosted API: proposed commit ladder + soft-throttle swap
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@flowmarket.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted commit uplift — need options and timing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We're seeing a material increase in nightly traffic for our browse and recommendations endpoints and need to lock in a higher monthly commit to avoid frequent throttles.

High level ask: can Redwood help us move from our current 1.2M token/month hosted commit to something in the 3–5M range for the next 6 months? Important constraints:
- We need a firm burst allowance for Black Friday week.
- Billing needs to be predictable (monthly invoice) and show per-token rate presuming the committed tier.
- We may want a short-term soft-throttle so we don't get immediate hard throttles while we test batching/kv-cache changes.

Can you share a few structured options (commit bands, effective per-token rates, burst pocket, and any minimum term changes)? Also please include an ops checklist for the onboarding change (routing, rate limits, and metrics to watch).

Attachments: none from us yet — I can share an internal usage extract if helpful.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering
FlowMarket
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@flowmarket.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted commit uplift — need options and timing

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely put together options that meet Black Friday burst needs and give you a predictable invoice cadence.

I'm looping in Marissa (contracts/ops) and Ben (commercial) to draft:
- a 6-month uplift path (3 tiers: nominal, elevated, and peak with pricing),
- burst pocket definition for the Black Friday window, and
- a soft-throttle policy (graceband + staged hard throttle) so your app sees graceful degradation rather than abrupt errors.

Quick Qs to make the pricing tight:
1) Do you want an upfront partial prepay for the commit (reduces the per-token rate)?
2) Approximately how many tokens/day are you seeing peak now vs. baseline (if you can send a CSV)?
3) Any regulatory or VPC requirements for the traffic in that timeframe?

I'll have a draft SOW and pricing grid today EOD PT.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@flowmarket.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted commit uplift — need options and timing

On Thu, Nov 4, 2027 at 10:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick Qs to make the pricing tight:
> 1) Do you want an upfront partial prepay for the commit (reduces the per-token rate)?
> 2) Approximately how many tokens/day are you seeing peak now vs. baseline (if you can send a CSV)?
> 3) Any regulatory or VPC requirements for the traffic in that timeframe?

Answers:
1) We can consider a one-month prepay to simplify accounting.
2) Baseline is roughly 40k tokens/day; peaks have spiked to ~220k tokens/day on recent campaigns. I'll attach our usage export.
3) No VPC requirement for this workload — just standard TLS and SOC2 controls.

Sending usage export as a separate message.

—Elena
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@flowmarket.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted commit uplift — need options and timing

Hi Elena, thanks for the CSV — helpful. I've attached a draft SOW and a pricing workbook with three structured bands we typically use for mid-market customers. Highlights:
- Option A (3M/month): 12% per-token discount w/ 1-month prepay; 48-hour SLA for availability; 100k burst pocket; soft-throttle at +10% over commit with 30-minute grace.
- Option B (4.5M/month): 20% per-token discount w/ 1-month prepay; 99.95% SLA; 250k burst pocket; soft-throttle with canary fallback to a cheaper model tier.
- Option C (5M/month): 24% per-token discount w/ 2-month prepay; 99.98% SLA; 500k burst pocket; dedicated capacity lanes (subject to Dedicated availability).

Ops checklist excerpt:
- Update routing policy to prefer cached prefixes + model-variant fallback for low-latency calls.
- Configure per-route rate limits and client-side retry/backoff.
- Define monitoring alerts (75% commit, 90% commit, burst usage).

Attachments: FM_Commit_Change_SOW.pdf, redwood-upgrade-pricing-v2.xlsx

If this looks directionally correct, Ben can pull together a short commercial term sheet and I can prepare the SOW for signature.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@flowmarket.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted commit uplift — pricing + term recommendations

Elena — quick commercial note from our side: based on the usage export and the Black Friday sensitivity, my recommended starting point is Option B (4.5M/month) with a 30-day prepay. Reasoning:
- Gives headroom for the campaign without the cost of dedicated capacity.
- Burst pocket at 250k should cover expected Black Friday surges if combined with prefix caching and temporary client-side queueing.
- We can include a one-time onboarding credit of $5k to offset engineering ramp.

If FlowMarket signs a 6-month commitment at Option B, the monthly invoice will show: committed tokens, per-token effective rate, and any consumed burst tokens billed at the overage rate defined in the SOW. We can add a clause for a mid-term commit review after month 3 to revisit rate bands.

I can get a redlined term sheet and DocuSign envelope ready today.

—Ben
Head of Commercial Programs | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@flowmarket.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2027 17:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted commit uplift — pricing + term recommendations

Thanks — Option B sounds like the right balance. Please send the DocuSign and I'll route to Procurement. A couple of small asks before signature:
- Add a defined Black Friday surge runbook (Ops steps + contact list).
- Include the 30-day mid-term review in the SOW language.
- Please note invoice to: FlowMarket, Attn: Procurement (procureops@flowmarket.com).

I'll expect the DocuSign link and a one-page runbook as attachments.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering, FlowMarket
